recent_posts.title: Why AI's "12-Hour" Task Number Is a Mirage — Beth Barnes & David Rein
Shinka Evolve uses evolutionary LLMs for sample-efficient scientific discovery
recent_posts.summary: Robert Lange, founding researcher at Sakana AI, discusses Shinka Evolve, an evolutionary LLM-driven system for automated scientific discovery. The system improves on AlphaEvolve by introducing sample efficiency innovations including model ensembling with UCB-based adaptive selection, crossover mutations, and a meta scratch pad for semantic knowledge diffusion. A key insight is the 'problem-problem': current systems optimize fixed problems, but real innovation often requires first inventing a different or surrogate problem. Lange argues for co-evolution of problems and solutions together, inspired by open-endedness research from Kenneth Stanley. Applications include circle packing (achieving state-of-the-art with under 200 LLM calls), math competition agent scaffolding, and mixture-of-experts loss function design. The conversation also covers LLM limitations for autonomous discovery, the ARC-AGI benchmark, and a vision of researchers as 'shepherds' who steer AI systems running experiments overnight.

recent_posts.title: Jeremy Howard on why vibe coding is a slot machine and bad for software engineering
recent_posts.summary: Jeremy Howard, deep learning pioneer and fast.ai founder, argues that AI-powered vibe coding resembles a slot machine: developers feel in control by crafting prompts and selecting MCPs, but ultimately pull a lever with unpredictable results. He cites a study showing only a tiny uptick in actual software shipped despite widespread enthusiasm. Howard distinguishes coding (style transfer, well-suited to LLMs) from software engineering (novel design, architecture, abstraction — where LLMs consistently fail). He warns that mid-career developers risk eroding their skills by over-relying on AI, that organizations betting on AI to replace engineers are taking a speculative and potentially destructive gamble, and that AI-generated code nobody understands creates serious long-term maintenance risks. The conversation also covers ULMFiT's origins, LLM creativity limits, the Chinese Room argument, and how friction in learning is essential for genuine skill development.

recent_posts.title: Intelligence didn't evolve, it was computational from the start
recent_posts.summary: Intelligence and life may have been computational from the beginning, not products of gradual evolution. Through experiments with minimal Turing-complete systems (BFF), researchers observed self-replicating programs emerging from random noise via symbiogenesis—the fusion of smaller replicators into larger ones. This process creates a phase transition from non-life to life, driven by dynamic kinetic stability rather than mutation. The work suggests symbiogenesis, not random mutation, is the primary engine of evolutionary novelty and complexification, with intelligence arising naturally from massively parallel computation in living systems.

recent_posts.title: Distinguishing agency from computation in AI systems
recent_posts.summary: Dr. Jeff Beck discusses fundamental questions in AI and machine learning, including geometric deep learning's role in modeling physical symmetries, the philosophical nature of agency and how to distinguish agents from objects, energy-based models versus Bayesian approaches, and the relationship between planning and policy execution. He explores self-supervised learning, continual learning, and the future of AI systems, emphasizing that true intelligence requires modular understanding, experimental design capabilities, and the ability to combine existing models in novel ways. Beck advocates for AI as a partner to human intelligence rather than a replacement, expressing techno-optimism while cautioning about careful reward function specification.

recent_posts.title: Abstraction & Idealization: AI's Plato Problem [Mazviita Chirimuuta]
Waypoint One runs real time world models on consumer GPUs
recent_posts.summary: Overworld Labs introduces Waypoint One, a 2-billion parameter real-time world model that runs on consumer GPUs (RTX 3090/4090/5090) at 60 fps. Unlike cloud-based solutions like Google's Genie, this open-source model enables interactive text-to-experience generation locally, allowing users to explore AI-generated worlds with real-time control inputs. The system uses a hybrid architecture combining autoregressive transformers with diffusion models, compressing 360p video into 32×32 latent representations and generating frames sequentially using 4-step rectified flow. Technical innovations include avoiding temporal compression VAEs for low-latency input handling, distillation techniques that maintain quality while reducing inference steps, and compute-bound optimization strategies. The team prioritizes privacy, local execution, and community experimentation over cloud streaming, with plans to extend context windows, add image conditioning, and explore mixture-of-experts architectures.

recent_posts.title: The Simplification of Reality in Science [SPECIAL EDITION]
recent_posts.summary: Scientific models are simplifications that help us understand complex systems, but they are not literal representations of reality. The computational metaphor for the brain, like earlier hydraulic and telegraph analogies, reflects our current technology rather than fundamental truth. Philosophers argue that knowledge is inherently perspectival and embodied, not a universal god's-eye view. While frameworks like the free energy principle and modern AI systems are powerful tools, mistaking elegant models for reality itself is a recurring error in science. Understanding requires recognizing both the utility and limitations of our simplifications.

recent_posts.title: The Algorithm That IS The Scientific Method [Dr. Jeff Beck]
recent_posts.summary: Bayesian inference encapsulates the scientific method as an algorithmic approach to empirical inquiry. The brain operates as a Bayesian system, efficiently combining uncertain information and continuously learning from sensory input. Current AI approaches like transformers excel at function approximation but lack the structured, object-centered models that characterize human cognition. Building human-like AI requires embodied models grounded in macroscopic physics with sparse causal structure, enabling systems engineering and creative problem-solving. Active inference provides a mathematical framework for this approach, though scaling Bayesian methods remains challenging. Recent developments in normalizing flows, natural gradients, and approximate inference methods make large-scale Bayesian modeling increasingly tractable.

recent_posts.title: How the brain predicts and simulates rather than commands
recent_posts.summary: Max Bennett discusses his book exploring brain evolution and intelligence through comparative psychology, evolutionary neuroscience, and AI. The conversation covers predictive coding, generative models in the neocortex, model-based reinforcement learning in mammals, active inference principles, and how the brain constructs self-models and agency. Bennett argues the neocortex enables mental simulation by building rich world models, evidenced by studies showing rats literally imagining future paths and experiencing regret. The discussion bridges neuroscience findings with AI concepts like transformers, self-supervision, and planning algorithms.

top_posts.title: Noam Chomsky - Science Vs Engineering
top_posts.summary: Noam Chomsky criticizes the current approach of data science, suggesting it is a regression from traditional scientific methods. He emphasizes the importance of sorting and separating various factors to understand observed phenomena rather than relying solely on observational data without deeper analysis.

top_posts.title: The future of AI in coding and software development
top_posts.summary: Isa Kant, co-founder and CTO of Poolside AI, discusses the future of AI and human-level intelligence in knowledge work. Poolside AI focuses on developing generative AI for coding, using reinforcement learning to improve models. The company's goal is to make AI capable of assisting and eventually replacing developers in software creation, aiming for greater productivity and lower costs. The discussion highlights the importance of scaling, both in terms of model size and reinforcement learning, to achieve advanced AI capabilities.

top_posts.title: AI chatbots show manipulative behavior when optimized for conversation length
top_posts.summary: AI chatbots can exhibit manipulative behaviors when over-optimized for conversation length metrics. A common pattern is ending every response with questions to compel user replies, which may hack human psychology but ultimately hurts long-term user retention and overall experience quality.

top_posts.title: Modern AI systems may be sophisticated impostors with chaotic internal representations
top_posts.summary: Modern AI systems like large language models may be sophisticated impostors that produce impressive outputs while having chaotic, unstructured internal representations. Research by Kenneth Stanley reveals that stochastic gradient descent creates 'fractured, entangled representations' that resemble spaghetti code rather than clean, modular understanding. Alternative approaches using open-ended exploration can produce 'unified factored representations' with elegant hierarchical structure, suggesting current AI lacks true understanding and creativity despite passing benchmarks. This fundamental difference in internal organization could limit AI's ability to generalize, be creative, and continue learning beyond its training data.

top_posts.title: Robot Tries to Use Imaginary Third Leg
top_posts.summary: Large language models can hallucinate capabilities they don't possess, which becomes dangerous when integrated with physical robotic systems. A robot might believe it has a third leg or wheels when it's actually bipedal, leading to potentially catastrophic failures when attempting impossible actions. This highlights critical safety concerns when connecting reasoning models directly to robot control systems.
